## Duke's conduct policies

Let's say we catch you:


::: incremental 
- If you are a first-time offender, your case goes to "faculty-student resolution";
- If you sign your name, you admit to wrongdoing, and agree to accept the policies outlined in my syllabus;
- If you do not re-offend, Duke promises that this first offense will not appear on your transcript and is not reportable outside the university.
:::

## Except... {.medium}

::: incremental 
- Medical school applicants are compelled to self-report any prior cases of misconduct, *even if* they are unreportable and do not appear on a transcript;
- This is what the AAMC calls an "[Institutional Action](https://students-residents.aamc.org/applying-medical-school-amcas/publication-chapters/institutional-action):"

    > If you were ever the recipient of any institutional action by any college or medical school for...a conduct violation, you must answer Yes...even if such action did not: interrupt your enrollment, require you to withdraw, or appear on your official transcripts.

- Duke prehealth advising has [a whole page](https://advising.duke.edu/prehealth/apply/comduct-violations/) on this.
:::

## Data science and statistical thinking

Before spring break...

-   **Data science**: the real-world *art* of transforming messy, imperfect, incomplete data into knowledge;

After spring break...

-   **Statistics**: the mathematical discipline of quantifying our uncertainty about that knowledge.

## Data preparation {.scrollable .small}

```{r}
survey <- survey |>
  rename(
    tue_classes = `How many classes do you have on Tuesdays?`,
    year = `What year are you?`
  ) |>
  mutate(
    tue_classes = case_when(
      tue_classes == "1 class, 1 lab, 1 volunteering session" ~ "2",
      tue_classes == "One" ~ "1",
      tue_classes == "Three" ~ "3",
      tue_classes == "Two" ~ "2",
      tue_classes == "Two in both days" ~ "2",
      tue_classes == "two" ~ "2",
      .default = tue_classes
    ),
    tue_classes = as.numeric(tue_classes),
    year = fct_relevel(year, "First-year", "Sophomore", "Junior", "Senior")
  ) |>
  select(tue_classes, year)
survey
```

## Data science {.medium}

1.  **Collection**: we won't seriously study this!

    -   **for us**: data importing (`read_csv`) or webscraping;

## A cautionary tale: Anscombe's quartet

```{r}
#| echo: false
anscombe_tidy <- anscombe |>
    mutate(observation = seq_len(n())) |>
    gather(key, value, -observation) |>
    separate(key, c("variable", "set"), 1, convert = TRUE) |>
    mutate(set = c("I", "II", "III", "IV")[set]) |>
    spread(variable, value)
```

::: columns
::: {.column width="25%"}
Dataset I

```{r}
#| echo: false
anscombe_tidy |>
  filter(set == "I") |>
  select(x, y)
```
:::

::: {.column width="25%"}
Dataset II

```{r}
#| echo: false
anscombe_tidy |>
  filter(set == "II") |>

```
:::

## A cautionary tale: Anscombe's quartet

```{r}
ggplot(anscombe_tidy, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ set) 
```

## A cautionary tale: Anscombe's quartet

```{r}
ggplot(anscombe_tidy, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ set) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)
```

## If you only looked at summary statistics...

```{r}
anscombe_tidy |>
  group_by(set) |>
  summarize(
    xbar = mean(x),
    ybar = mean(y),
    sx = sd(x),
    sy = sd(y),
    r = cor(x, y)
  )
```

# Study guide 

## Can you match these...

```{r}
#| label: simulate-data
#| echo: false
set.seed(8675309)

banana = function(A, B, C1, C2, N, keep = 10, init = 10)
{
  R=init*keep+N*keep
  x1=x2=0
  bimat=matrix(double(2*N),ncol=2)
  for (r in 1:R) {
    x1=rnorm(1,mean=(B*x2+C1)/(A*(x2^2)+1),sd=sqrt(1/(A*(x2^2)+1)))
    x2=rnorm(1,mean=(B*x2+C2)/(A*(x1^2)+1),sd=sqrt(1/(A*(x1^2)+1)))
    if (r>init*keep && r%%keep==0) {
        mkeep=r/keep; bimat[mkeep-init,]=c(x1,x2)
    }
  }

  return(bimat)
}

n <- 2500
p <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)

z1 <- mvrnorm(n, numeric(2), 0.1 * cbind(c(1, 0.5), c(0.5, 1)))

z2 <- mvrnorm(n, c(-0.5, 0), 0.05 * cbind(c(1, 0), c(0, 2))) * p + 
      mvrnorm(n, c(0.5, 0), 0.05 * cbind(c(1, 0), c(0, 2))) * (1 - p)
z3 <- cbind(rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = 0.35), 
            0.5 * rexp(n) - 1)
z4 <- 0.6 * scale(banana(A = 2, B = 0, C1 = 3, C2 = 3, n))
z5 <- cbind(runif(n, -1, 1),
            runif(n, -1, 1))
z6 <- mvrnorm(n, c(-0.5, 0.5), 0.05 * cbind(c(1, 0), c(0, 1))) * p + 
      mvrnorm(n, c(0.5, -0.5), 0.05 * cbind(c(1, 0), c(0, 1))) * (1 - p)



z <- tibble(
  plot_no = c(rep("2", n), rep("3", n), rep("4", n), 
              rep("5", n), rep("6", n), rep("7", n)),
  x = c(z1[,1], z2[,1], z3[,1], z4[,1], z5[,1], z6[,1]),
  y = c(z1[,2], z2[,2], z3[,2], z4[,2], z5[,2], z6[,2])
)
```

```{r}
#| label: simulated-data-scatterplots
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-asp: 0.66
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-align: center
ggplot(z, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.25) +
  facet_wrap(~plot_no) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  coord_fixed()
```

## ...with these?

```{r}
#| label: simulated-data-histograms
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-asp: 1.25
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-align: center
z_long <- z |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(x, y),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    plot_no = case_when(
      plot_no == "2"   ~ "Histogram pair e",
      plot_no == "3"  ~ "Histogram pair d",
      plot_no == "4" ~ "Histogram pair b",
      plot_no == "5"  ~ "Histogram pair a",
      plot_no == "6"  ~ "Histogram pair c",
      plot_no == "7"  ~ "Histogram pair f",
    )
  )

ggplot(z_long, aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  facet_grid(
    plot_no ~ variable, 
    scales = "free_y",
    switch = "y"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(
    strip.placement = "outside",
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
  )
```

## Can you match these...

```{r}
#| label: simulate-data-2
#| echo: false
set.seed(8675309)
n <- 2500
p <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)

x1 <- r(UnivarMixingDistribution(Norm(mean = -2.5, sd = 0.1),
                                 Norm(mean = -1.5, sd = 0.2), 
                                 Norm(mean = -0, sd = 0.25),
                                 Norm(mean = +1.5, sd = 0.2),
                                 Norm(mean = +2.5, sd = 0.1),
                                 mixCoeff = c(0.05, 0.2, .5, 0.2, 0.05))
        )(n)
x2 <- r(UnivarMixingDistribution(Norm(mean = -2, sd = 0.5), 
                                 Norm(mean = -0, sd = 1.25),
                                 mixCoeff = c(0.65, 0.35))
        )(n)
x3 <- runif(n, min = -4, max = 4)
x4 <- -4 + 8 * rbeta(n, 0.1, 0.1)
x5 <- rnorm(n, mean = -2, sd = 0.75)
x6 <- r(UnivarMixingDistribution(Norm(mean = 2, sd = 0.75), 
                                 Norm(mean = -0.5, sd = 1),
                                 mixCoeff = c(0.65, 0.35))
        )(n)

z <- tibble(
  plot_no = c(rep("08", n), rep("09", n), rep("10", n), 
              rep("11", n), rep("12", n), rep("13", n)),
  x = c(x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6)
)
```


```{r}
#| label: simulated-data-densities
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-align: center
ggplot(z, aes(x = x)) +
  geom_density(fill = "grey") +
  facet_wrap(~plot_no) +
  xlim(-4, 4)
```

```{r}
z |>
  mutate(
    plot_no = case_when(
      plot_no == "08"   ~ "Boxplot f",
      plot_no == "09"  ~ "Boxplot a",
      plot_no == "10" ~ "Boxplot b",
      plot_no == "11"  ~ "Boxplot e",
      plot_no == "12"  ~ "Boxplot c",
      plot_no == "13"  ~ "Boxplot d",
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = x)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.1) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~plot_no
  ) +
  xlim(-4, 4) + 
  #scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  #labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(
    axis.ticks.y = element_line(color = "white"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(color = "white")
  )

  #)
```

## Yes you can

If you know how the box is drawn:

::: incremental 
- The line inside the box is the median (50% quantile);
- The left edge is the 25% quantile;
- The right edge is the 75% quantile;
- The box spans the middle 50% of the data;
- The whiskers and dots span the entire range of the data;
:::

. . .

Boxplots display center, spread, and (a)symmetry, but *not* modality.

## Whence the box? {.medium .scrollable}

The middle of the box is the **median**. 50% of the data are below, and 50% are above:

```{r}
#| echo: false

df <- gerrymander

df_long <- rbind(
  transform(df, panel = "Histogram"),
  transform(df, panel = "Box plot")
)

df_long$panel <- factor(df_long$panel, levels = c("Histogram", "Box plot"))

med <- median(df$trump16)

ggplot(df_long, aes(x = trump16)) +
  # Histogram (top)
  geom_histogram(
    data = subset(df_long, panel == "Histogram"),
    bins = 30, color = "white", fill = "grey70"
  ) +
  
  # Boxplot (bottom)
  geom_boxplot(
    data = subset(df_long, panel == "Box plot"),
    aes(y = 0),
    width = 0.2,
    outlier.shape = NA
  ) +
  
  # Median line in both panels
  geom_vline(xintercept = med, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", linewidth = 2) +
  
  facet_grid(rows = vars(panel), scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(NULL, breaks = NULL) +
  labs(x = "x") +
  theme_minimal()

```
